Cc: procurement@cascadia.ai
Date: 2025-12-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Order Form: SLA and Maintenance Windows (Cascadia.ai)

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and our platform team reviewed Redwood's order form and have a few non-standard asks on SLA/support before we can move to a PO: 

- Uptime: require 99.99% for the hosted offering.
- Response times: P1 initial acknowledgement within 15 minutes, P2 within 2 hours.
- Maintenance windows: no scheduled maintenance that impacts production during our core business hours (Mon–Fri 08:00–18:00 PT). Prefer maintenance windows to be limited to 4 hours and not more than twice/month.
- Service credits: automatic crediting for any availability violations, with a minimum payout threshold of 1% of monthly invoice and no single-event cap below 10% of monthly fees.

Attaching our SLA ask (Cascadia_RFP_SLA_ask.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these as-is or propose the closest compromise? Procurement would like a redline of the order form if possible.

Best,
Anna Park
Head of Platform Ops
Cascadia.ai

Subject: Fwd: Order Form: SLA and Maintenance Windows (Cascadia.ai) — quick position

Team — forwarding Cascadia's asks. High-level thoughts:

- 99.99% for hosted is a stretch; standard hosted SLA is 99.95%. Dedicated pools we can commit to 99.99 with reserved capacity.
- 15min P1 ack for hosted is aggressive. We can offer 30 min initial response for hosted with a 15 min target for Dedicated + premium support add-on.
- Maintenance window restrictions: we can agree to avoid scheduled maintenance during client core hours, but we need a 72-hour notice and the ability to run critical security patches with a shorter notice (emergency window). Recommend carving out an exception for emergency security fixes.
- Credits: prefer capping credits to monthly invoice (standard). We can accept a lower single-event cap than 10% for strategic deals — suggest negotiating to 20% monthly cap with escalation clauses.

I'll draft a redline order form that attempts to split differences (hosted: 99.95% + upgrade path to 99.99 for reserved). Please review attached draft (redline_order_form_v1.docx) and add legal edits.

— Marcus
Director, Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Folks — reviewed Marcus' draft. My suggested legal positions: 

1) Availability metric: keep hosted at 99.95% in the MSA, allow customer to purchase Dedicated or Reserved capacity options at 99.99% in the Order Form. Add explicit language that uptime is measured monthly and excludes Customer-caused outages and scheduled maintenance per Section X.

2) Service credits: accept automatic crediting but cap cumulative credits to the greater of (i) 100% of the monthly fees for the impacted service, or (ii) a fixed dollar cap tied to the initial term for large enterprise deals. Do not agree to per-event pools below 10% without compensation (we can offer a phased ramp).

3) Response times: define "initial response" vs "mitigation". For hosted we should keep "initial response" at 30 minutes for P1s, with a commitment to provide continuous updates until mitigation. For Dedicated/excellent support tiers, we can accept the 15-minute SLA.

4) Maintenance: define scheduled maintenance as activities with >=72 hours' notice. Emergency maintenance (e.g., CVE patching) may be performed with shorter notice; require post-event notification and a mitigation plan. Block maintenance during customer's core hours if requested, but require an upper bound on number of blackout-free weeks (we cannot guarantee zero maintenance for indefinite periods).

5) Escalation & audit: include a clause for joint postmortems and right to audit incident logs for material breaches. Request SOC2 evidence before signature (redact where necessary).

I've made inline edits in orderform_redline_legal.docx (attached). Recommend we propose a split: hosted 99.95% / dedicated 99.99%, hosted P1=30min / Dedicated P1=15min, credits capped to monthly fees with escalation path to increase for multi-year commitments.

— Lauren
Sr. Counsel, Redwood

Anna —

Thanks for the clear asks and the attached doc. We want to get Cascadia live with Redwood — below is a pragmatic compromise that aligns with our operational guarantees and addresses your concerns: 

- Uptime: Hosted: 99.95% monthly. Option to execute a Dedicated Reserved Capacity Order Form for 99.99% with a 3–6 week provisioning lead time.
- Response times: Hosted P1 initial response within 30 minutes (continuous updates until mitigation). Dedicated + Enterprise Support: P1 initial response within 15 minutes.
- Maintenance windows: We will not schedule planned maintenance during 08:00–18:00 PT Mon–Fri for the first 90 days post-production cutover. After 90 days, we will provide scheduled maintenance windows outside core hours with >=72 hours' notice and limit scheduled maintenance impact to a maximum of 8 hours per calendar month (split across up to two events). Emergency security patches may be applied with less notice; we will notify and provide a post-action report.
- Service credits: Automatic crediting for availability violations. Credits will be applied monthly and capped at the greater of (i) 100% of the monthly recurring fees for the impacted service or (ii) a fixed cap we can negotiate for multi-year deals. We can discuss higher single-event caps for an expanded commercial commitment.

Next steps: Attached is a redlined Order Form that reflects the positions above (redline_order_form_v1.docx). If this is acceptable in principle, can procurement confirm which path they prefer (hosted vs. dedicated)? If dedicated, we'll route for capacity provisioning and present a tightening to the SLA. For SOC2 and compliance, please share the specific artifacts you need and we'll provide the appropriate report (we have a clean SOC2 Type II report).

Proposed timeline: agreement on SLA redlines by 2025-12-11 to hit a Jan production target.

— Marcus
Director, Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the redline. The compromise outlined below is acceptable in principle. A few small asks before procurement will sign: 

1) Maintenance notice: Can we get 72 hours' advance notice for any planned maintenance that could impact production (rather than the 72 hours only after the 90-day window)? We understand emergency patches are excluded.
2) Credits: we can accept the monthly cap language if there is an explicit inflation-adjusted floor for the first 12 months (Cascadia will not accept a de minimis floor under 1% for auto-crediting).
3) SOC2: please attach the report and the dates covered. We need the report before the PO.

I'll circulate the redline to procurement as soon as those three items are in the order form. Attaching our SOC/req list to this thread for reference and our SOC2 stub (SOC2_report_stub.pdf).

If you can update the order form today with the maintenance notice language and SOC2 attachment, we can aim to exchange signatures early next week.
